 CJ Olive Young to launch first colour cosmetics store in Seoul’s Hongdae
 New brands make up 26% of the store's cosmetics labels.  
 South Korean beauty retailer CJ Olive Young will open its first colour cosmetics store, COLOR GROUND Hongdae, on 20 November in Seogyo-dong, Mapo-gu, Seoul.
 The four-storey store covers about 575 square metres and will sell products from established and emerging Korean makeup brands.
 The launch is part of Olive Young's strategy to expand its colour cosmetics business and promote Korean makeup brands internationally.
 South Korea exported $1.11b worth of colour cosmetics from January to September this year, compared with $8.72b in skincare exports, according to the Ministry of Food and Drug Safety.
 The global colour cosmetics market is estimated to reach $105.2b this year.
 Olive Young's colour cosmetics category recorded a compound annual sales growth rate of 36% over the past five years.
 The retailer chose Hongdae because of its young consumer base and international visitor traffic. From January to October, shoppers in their teens and twenties accounted for more than half of sales at Olive Young stores in the area, while international customers made up 84%.
 The store will group products by type, formulation and function rather than by brand, allowing shoppers to compare products across different labels.
 New brands making their Olive Young debut account for 26% of the colour cosmetics brands at the store. A dedicated Rookie Zone on the third floor will showcase emerging labels.
 The outlet will also offer makeup trials, personalised colour analysis and video tutorials. Services include QUICK TOUCH UP MOOD, which lets shoppers try makeup looks suited to their facial features, and SKIN SCAN COLOR FIT, a colour analysis service.
 Olive Young also plans to promote functional products such as lip conditioners, lash care products and makeup fixers to international consumers as an entry point for Korean colour cosmetics.
